pages.text: This is the story of Allah's mercy to His servant Zakariya (peace be upon him), and in it is a lesson for those who reflect. Zakariya called on his Lord in secret, so that his du'a would be more sincere to Allah and closer to being answered.

He said in his du'a: ﴿رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ ٱلۡعَظۡمُ مِنِّي وَٱشۡتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأۡسُ شَيۡبٗا وَلَمۡ أَكُنۢ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيّٗا﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'My Lord, my bones have grown weak and my hair has turned white, and I have never been let down in my du'a to You, my Lord.' His wife could not have children, so he asked his Lord to give him a child from Him, to inherit prophethood and to be pleasing.

Allah gave him glad tidings of a boy named Yahya, a name no one was given before him. Zakariya wondered how he could have a boy when he had reached the very end of old age, and his Lord told him that this was easy for Him, for He had created him before, when he was nothing. And Allah gave him a sign: that he would not be able to speak to people for three nights and their days, while he was healthy and well.
Zakariya came out to his people from his place of prayer, and signalled to them to glorify Allah morning and evening, in thanks to Him.

Yahya was born, and when he was old enough to understand, Allah said to him: ﴿يَٰيَحۡيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِقُوَّةٖۖ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'O Yahya, hold firmly to the Book.' He commanded him to take the Torah with effort and care: to memorise its words, understand its meanings and act on it. And Allah gave him wisdom and good understanding while he was still young, and mercy and love from Him.

Among the lessons of these verses is that Allah showed mercy to His servant Zakariya and answered his du'a. The lesson is also in the words of Allah the Exalted about Yahya: ﴿وَبَرَّۢا بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيّٗا﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'And dutiful to his parents, and he was not arrogant or disobedient.' He was dutiful to his parents and obeyed them, never arrogant, and never disobedient to his Lord or to his parents. And peace from Allah be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.
